```sql fiscal_years
select distinct fiscal_year
from volteo.income_statement
order by fiscal_year desc
```

<Dropdown data={fiscal_years} name=fy value=fiscal_year title="Fiscal year" defaultValue="2025"/>

```sql headline
select
    sum(case when label = 'Net revenue'  then value end) as net_revenue,
    sum(case when label = 'Gross profit' then value end) as gross_profit,
    sum(case when label = 'EBITDA'       then value end) as ebitda,
    sum(case when label = 'Net income'   then value end) as net_income,
    sum(case when label = 'Gross profit' then value end)
      / nullif(sum(case when label = 'Net revenue' then value end), 0) as gm_pct,
    sum(case when label = 'Net income'   then value end)
      / nullif(sum(case when label = 'Net revenue' then value end), 0) as ni_pct
from volteo.income_statement
where report_id = 'IS_MGMT' and fiscal_year = ${inputs.fy.value}
```

## Statement

Fiscal year runs July&ndash;June, so P01 is July and the Christmas peak falls at
P05&ndash;P06 &mdash; mid-year, not at year end.

```sql statement
select
    sort_order,
    label,
    max(is_subtotal) as is_subtotal,
    sum(case when entity = 'US01' then value end) as us01,
    sum(case when entity = 'DE01' then value end) as de01,
    sum(case when entity = 'ES01' then value end) as es01,
    sum(case when entity = 'UK01' then value end) as uk01,
    sum(case when entity = 'ELIM' then value end) as elim,
    sum(case when entity = 'GRP'  then value end) as topside,
    sum(value) as consolidated
from volteo.income_statement
where report_id = 'IS_MGMT' and fiscal_year = ${inputs.fy.value}
group by sort_order, label
order by sort_order
```

<div class="stmt-scroll">
<table class="stmt">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th class="lbl">USD thousands</th>
      <th>US01</th><th>DE01</th><th>ES01</th><th>UK01</th>
      <th>Elim.</th><th>Topside</th><th class="grp">Consolidated</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
  {#each statement as row}
    <tr class:subtotal={row.is_subtotal === 1} class:final={row.label === 'Net income'}>
      <th class="lbl">{row.label}</th>
      {#each ['us01','de01','es01','uk01','elim','topside','consolidated'] as key}
        <td
          class:neg={row[key] < -0.5}
          class:grp={key === 'consolidated'}
        >{row[key] == null || Math.abs(row[key]) < 500
            ? '—'
            : row[key] < 0
              ? '(' + Math.round(Math.abs(row[key]) / 1000).toLocaleString('en-US') + ')'
              : Math.round(row[key] / 1000).toLocaleString('en-US')}</td>
      {/each}
    </tr>
  {/each}
  </tbody>
</table>
</div>

Consolidation needs no special handling: eliminations and topside journals are rows in
`fact_gl` under the `ELIM` and `GRP` entities, so the consolidated column is simply every
entity summed.

## Where the result comes from month to month

P05 and P06 (November, December) carry the Black Friday and Christmas peak. Loss-making
months inside a profitable year are normal and deliberate.

```sql monthly
select entity, period_key, result
from volteo.monthly_result
where fiscal_year = ${inputs.fy.value}
order by period_key
```

<LineChart data={monthly} x=period_key y=result series=entity yFmt='$#,##0,"k"' title="Monthly result by entity"/>

## Margins against the configured narrative

Sign and trend are configured, not emergent. The generator calibrates each entity to a
target band by scaling only discretionary baselines, leaving seasonality and noise
untouched.

```sql margins
select entity, arc, gm_target, gm_actual, ni_target, ni_actual
from volteo.margins
where fiscal_year = ${inputs.fy.value}
order by entity
```

<DataTable data={margins} rows=all>
    <Column id=entity title="Entity"/>
    <Column id=arc title="Configured arc"/>
    <Column id=gm_target title="GM target" fmt='0.0%'/>
    <Column id=gm_actual title="GM actual" fmt='0.0%'/>
    <Column id=ni_target title="NI target" fmt='0.0%'/>
    <Column id=ni_actual title="NI actual" fmt='0.0%'/>
</DataTable>

UK01 is a configured turnaround: it starts loss-making and crosses zero. Its earlier year
also covers a partial period, because it consolidates only from its acquisition month —
the jump between years is an M&A scope effect, not organic growth.

## Injected defects, surfaced

These are deliberate. `v_data_quality` exposes them as a monitorable table so an alert
can watch them rather than a reader discovering them by accident.

```sql defects
select issue, entity, fiscal_year, period_key, rows_affected, amount
from volteo.data_quality
where fiscal_year = ${inputs.fy.value}
order by issue, period_key
```

<DataTable data={defects} rows=12>
    <Column id=issue title="Issue"/>
    <Column id=entity title="Entity"/>
    <Column id=period_key title="Period"/>
    <Column id=rows_affected title="Rows" fmt='#,##0'/>
    <Column id=amount title="Amount" fmt='$#,##0'/>
</DataTable>

- **`untagged_product`** — about 0.5% of revenue rows carry `UNASSIGNED` instead of a real
  product. Revenue by product will not sum to total revenue. Note that `UNASSIGNED` is
  *not* `~NA~`: the latter means the dimension does not apply at all, which is correct
  for payroll and production variances.
- **`ic_partner_missing`** — one UK purchase from DE01 loses its partner tag each year, so
  it escapes automatic elimination and overstates group cost.

## Non-controlling interest

```sql nci
select entity, fiscal_year, nci_pct, entity_net_income,
       nci_before_adjustment, nci_unrealised_adjustment, nci_net_income
from volteo.nci
order by entity, fiscal_year
```

<DataTable data={nci} rows=all>
    <Column id=entity title="Entity"/>
    <Column id=fiscal_year title="FY"/>
    <Column id=nci_pct title="NCI %" fmt='0%'/>
    <Column id=entity_net_income title="Entity NI" fmt='$#,##0'/>
    <Column id=nci_before_adjustment title="20% share" fmt='$#,##0'/>
    <Column id=nci_unrealised_adjustment title="Unrealised profit adj." fmt='$#,##0'/>
    <Column id=nci_net_income title="NCI" fmt='$#,##0'/>
</DataTable>

ES01 is 80% owned. The minority's share of profit is more than offset by its share of
unrealised intercompany profit eliminated on closing stock, so the line lands negative —
driven by `closing_stock_share: 0.32` in the industry pack.
